title: 3.1 A 121.3dB-DR, 115dB-PSNR, Digital-Input Capacitive-Feedback Class-D Audio Amplifier with Double-Sided Voltage-Boosting (DSVB) Modulation
problem: Class-D audio amplifiers are limited in output power by battery voltage; prior approaches achieve boost via 2-stage DC-DC conversion (inefficient, ~80%) or single-stage buck-boost (limited dynamic range), struggling to combine high dynamic range (>120dB) with high efficiency and small form-factor.
motivation: Battery-powered high-end audio devices require >120dB dynamic range and high efficiency while minimizing inductor count and PCB footprint.
method: The amplifier combines three techniques in a single power stage: a buck-boost converter (a circuit that can increase or decrease voltage to boost power output), a noise-reduction circuit using capacitor feedback (the chopper-amplifier technique), and just one external inductor. This integrated single-stage design achieves a 121.3dB dynamic range—ability to accurately reproduce very quiet and very loud sounds together—at 87% efficiency, with only 13% power loss. By combining voltage conversion, noise reduction, and power delivery in one stage instead of separating them, the design is both smaller and more efficient than previous approaches that required multiple conversion stages.
key_novelty: The core innovation is a single-inductor circuit using flexible voltage boosting (DSVB) and capacitor-feedback noise reduction in one power stage to achieve both high sound quality (121.3dB dynamic range) and high efficiency (87%).
contributions: 121.3dB dynamic range (highest reported for audio amplifiers) via capacitive-feedback elimination of resistive-thermal-noise
115dB PSNR with single off-chip inductor (vs. two in prior capacitive-feedback designs)
87% single-stage power-delivery efficiency with voltage boost capability
primary_theme: Ultra-high-DR Class-D audio amplifier with single-inductor boost.
